# Results -- Study 507 (Cross-Sectional-Momentum) on real yfinance panel

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Protocol: Jegadeesh-Titman (1993)
12-1 relative strength -- rank the basket by trailing 12-month return skipping the most recent
month, long the top fraction (winners), short the bottom (losers), equal-weight, dollar-neutral,
rebalance monthly, hold one month. One execution lag (form on the month-end close, hold the next
month). As-of **2026-06-26**.*

## Data stamp

| Frame | Shape | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|
| Prices (daily adjusted-close) | 3424 days x 38 tickers | `e038fa42cc02` |
| Period covered | 2012-05-18 -- 2025-12-30 | -- |
| Monthly bars | 164 | -- |
| WML holding months | 151 (2013-05 -- 2025-11) | -- |

**Source:** yfinance daily adjusted-close (auto_adjust=True). Basket: 38 large-cap survivor
names (a fixed ~40-name large-cap list; NVDA/ABBV dropped on a transient fetch failure; the
common window starts mid-2012 because META and V list late). One-way cost 10bps/leg per
rebalance + 50bps/yr short borrow.

**Survivorship bias -- named on the SIGNAL axis (not hidden in tradability):** the basket is
names *still trading in 2026*. The loser leg's natural short candidates -- firms that trended
down into delisting or bankruptcy -- are absent by construction. Survivorship inflates a
momentum premium *more* than most factors because the deleted names are precisely the persistent
losers a momentum short would have harvested. Any WML premium reported here is an **upper bound**.

## Synthetic positive control (engine faithfulness -- NOT a real-tape claim)

A deterministic synthetic panel with a planted persistent relative-strength drift. The engine
must score ~0 at the null and rise monotonically as the planted drift grows.

| Planted drift | WML mean (ann) | HAC *t* |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 0.00 (null) | +6.5% | +1.47 |
| 0.15 | +17.4% | +4.00 |
| 0.30 | +40.3% | +7.88 |
| 0.50 | +71.3% | +12.50 |

Monotone in the planted drift; across 20 random seeds the null mean *t* is **-0.07** (not the
single-seed +1.47 above) and only 10% of seeds exceed |t|>2 -- a faithful, well-sized detector.
**This is a power check only; it is never cited to support the real-tape stamp.**

## The honest test -- real WML on the survivor basket

### Quintile sort (top/bottom 20%, ~8 names per leg)

| Statistic | Gross | Net (costs + borrow) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Mean return (ann) | **-0.34%/yr** | -1.43%/yr |
| Vol (ann) | 16.2% | 16.2% |
| Sharpe (ann) | -0.021 | -0.089 |
| **HAC t-stat** | **-0.072** | -0.306 |
| Hit rate (months > 0) | 54.3% | -- |
| Max drawdown | -44.9% | -- |
| Worst month | -17.7% | -- |
| Avg turnover | 24.8%/mo | -- |
| **Placebo p-value** | **0.545** | -- |

### Decile sort (top/bottom 10%, ~4 names per leg)

| Statistic | Gross | Net (costs + borrow) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Mean return (ann) | **+1.24%/yr** | +0.02%/yr |
| Sharpe (ann) | +0.054 | +0.001 |
| **HAC t-stat** | **+0.197** | +0.004 |
| Hit rate (months > 0) | 57.6% | -- |
| Max drawdown | -53.5% | -- |
| Worst month | -24.6% | -- |
| Avg turnover | 30.0%/mo | -- |
| **Placebo p-value** | **0.376** | -- |

- The quintile WML earns **-0.34%/yr** gross at HAC *t* = **-0.072** -- statistically
  indistinguishable from zero, sign *negative*. The placebo p-value of **0.545** says the real
  mean is no better than a coin-flip among label-shuffled nulls.
- The decile WML nudges to **+1.24%/yr** gross (HAC *t* = +0.197), but on only ~4 names per leg
  this is noise, not signal -- the placebo p-value (0.376) still does not clear any bar, and the
  net return collapses to **+0.02%/yr** once you pay 10bps/leg + 50bps borrow.
- **Both legs are winners.** The winner leg earns ~+16.2%/yr and the loser leg ~+16.5%/yr: in a
  basket of survivors that all compounded for a decade, sorting on past return separates almost
  nothing. This is the survivorship channel made visible -- the loser leg never contains the
  trending-to-zero names a real momentum short would profit from.

| Year | WML | Year | WML |
|---|--:|---|--:|
| 2013 | +1.1% | 2020 | -2.7% |
| 2014 | -4.1% | 2021 | -23.5% |
| 2015 | +26.0% | 2022 | +4.8% |
| 2016 | -26.7% | 2023 | -0.3% |
| 2017 | +28.2% | 2024 | +22.7% |
| 2018 | +2.1% | 2025 | -29.6% |
| 2019 | +3.1% | | |

The sign flips violently year to year (+28% in 2017, -30% in 2025) -- the classic momentum-crash
left tail with none of the long-run premium to compensate on this small, modern, survivor basket.

## Verdict

- **Signal -- NONE.** Quintile WML HAC *t* = -0.072 (placebo p = 0.545); decile *t* = +0.197
  (placebo p = 0.376). Neither sort distinguishes from zero, and the survivorship bias -- named
  on the SIGNAL axis -- means even these flat numbers are upper bounds. The synthetic control
  proves the engine *would* find momentum if it were there; the real basket simply does not carry
  it. Literature support (Jegadeesh-Titman 1993) is strong but, per house rules, prior alone is
  WEAK at most and the real tape here lands NONE.
- **Tradability -- MIRAGE.** Best-case net return +0.02%/yr (decile) with a -53.5% drawdown and
  30%/mo turnover; the quintile is outright negative net. There is nothing to trade.
- **Decile vs quintile (3rd axis) -- BUSTED.** Tightening the sort from quintile to decile did
  not surface an edge -- it traded a slightly-negative number for a slightly-positive one inside
  the noise band, at the cost of thinner legs (4 names), more turnover and a deeper drawdown.
  Concentration does not rescue momentum on a small survivor basket.
